instruction:
Read docs/TASK_MEGATRON_V4.md FIRST (in your context): sections 2.1-2.3 are the contract, section 3 lists the examples your test must prove. Every name you need is there or below; do not invent names, keys, numbers or files. Python 3.9-compatible syntax (typing.List/Dict/Optional/Tuple; no `match`, no `X | Y`), standard library only. Tests are unittest, `maxDiff = None` in every TestCase, `msg=` on every assertion, one test method per numbered example, each test's docstring names the example (e.g. `D example 4`). Fixtures are loaded from `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "fixtures")`; never modify them. Read the 30 logins of each page FROM the fixture (`[i["login"] for i in data["items"]]`) and compare whole lists; the spec's spot values (first three, index 29) are extra assertions, not the expected list. No test opens a network connection: no urlopen, no sockets.

A `.headers.txt` fixture is parsed in the test as: skip the first line (status line), strip each line, skip empty lines, split each remaining line at the first ": " into name and value (LF endings). The fake transport is a plain synchronous function `fake(url, headers)` keyed by the exact URL string, returning `(200, dict(parsed_headers), fixture_bytes)` (read the .json file in binary mode), appending every url to a list; an unknown URL returns `(404, {}, b'{"message": "Not Found"}')`. It is called from a worker thread by GitHubClient (run_in_executor). The client under test is always the real `GitHubClient(token="x", transport=fake, ...)` from megatron.github_client. Run coroutines with `asyncio.run`. U1 = "https://api.github.com/search/users?q=followers%3A%3E5000&per_page=30" (page 1 is served here), U2 = "https://api.github.com/search/users?q=followers%3A%3E5000&per_page=30&page=2" (page 2), and the empty query "followers:>100000000" is served at "https://api.github.com/search/users?q=followers%3A%3E100000000&per_page=30" with search_empty.json and search_empty.headers.txt.

## Search module (P, Q, D)

Write `megatron/search.py` (new) exactly as spec section 2.3 describes: `encode_query(query)`, `search_url(query, per_page=30)`, `parse_search_page(data)`, `async def discover_logins(client, query, pages, per_page=30)`. Import only `from megatron.github_client import API_ROOT, parse_next_link` from the package, plus typing; NO urllib of any kind (the network guard greps `urllib` in every module but github_client.py), so encode_query percent-encodes the UTF-8 bytes by hand: bytes of A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ kept, every other byte as '%%%02X'. discover_logins: if pages < 1 raise ValueError before touching anything. Otherwise keep `original = client.transport`, set `client.transport` to a wrapper `(url, headers) -> original(url, headers)` that stores the response's `link` header (case-insensitive name lookup, None when absent) and returns the triple unchanged; restore `client.transport = original` in `finally`. Loop: url = search_url(query, per_page); for each page `data = await client.fetch_json(url)`; `page = parse_search_page(data)` (call the module-global name, never a local alias, so a later redefinition in the module takes effect); extend logins; total_count from the FIRST page; incomplete_results = True if any page's is; count pages; stop when pages reached or `parse_next_link(stored_link)` is None, else url = that next URL verbatim. Never build a URL from a page number. Return {"logins", "total_count", "incomplete_results", "pages"}. parse_search_page returns {"logins": [item["login"] for item in data["items"]], "total_count": data["total_count"], "incomplete_results": bool(data["incomplete_results"])}.

Write `tests/test_search.py` proving spec section 3 examples P.1-P.4, Q.1-Q.2 and D.1-D.6 (12 test methods). Use `from megatron import search` and call `search.<name>` at call time. D.4: page 1 headers with `x-ratelimit-remaining` replaced by "0"; `GitHubClient(token="x", transport=fake, sleep=rec, clock=lambda: 1790599575)` where `async def rec(seconds)` appends `(seconds, len(urls_seen_so_far))` to a list: expect exactly `[(60, 1)]` (one sleep of 60 after the first request, before the second), then `client.rate_limit == {"limit": 10, "remaining": 8, "reset": 1790599635}`. D.5: after a successful pages=2 call `client.transport is fake`; with only U1 routed, pages=2 raises GitHubError with .status 404 and afterwards `client.transport is fake`. The acceptance appends a mutant to search.py that reverses each page's logins inside parse_search_page and requires your tests to FAIL on it.
